statusNote: Internal binding policy for claim classification and approval. It does not authorise any public publication. No claim is currently approved for public use; MC-14 publication authorization is NONE. The policy is compatible with MC-03's A/C/P/X classes but adds explicit audience and publication-status gates, and the stricter gate prevails over any inherited allowance.

claimClasses.name: Allowed in the specified context
claimClasses.definition: Supported by recorded facts and not conflicting with current governance.
claimClasses.audienceGate: INTERNAL_DOCUMENTATION_ONLY unless a separate public gate explicitly authorises publication
claimClasses.publicationRequirement: No evidence artefact required; context and audience must be stated
claimClasses.examples: Internal concept descriptions, definitions, edition inclusions that are already recorded in the product contracts.

claimClasses.name: Conditional
claimClasses.definition: May only be used after the named evidence requirement and approval are satisfied.
claimClasses.audienceGate: INTERNAL_DRAFT until evidence exists; PUBLIC after evidence and approval
claimClasses.publicationRequirement: Evidence record attached to the claim, approver sign-off, release gate open
claimClasses.examples: Tested compatibility, licensed data, measured performance, audited security.

claimClasses.name: Prohibited in the current state
claimClasses.definition: Unsupported or conflicting with an active blocker; no evidence route is currently satisfied.
claimClasses.publicationRequirement: Cannot be published while the named blocker is open; requires a policy amendment after evidence
claimClasses.examples: Availability, stock, final prices, certification, guarantees of alerts or performance.

claimClasses.name: Prohibited absolutely
claimClasses.publicationRequirement: No evidence route exists in this programme
claimClasses.examples: Invented certifications, customers, testimonials, awards, insurance, safety-of-life guarantees, autonomous control.

publicationStatusVocabulary.meaning: May appear in internal planning documents only; not customer-facing and not indexed.
May not appear on any public surface, channel, package, manual, proposal or store listing.
Publication is conditional on the named evidence and approval; not currently authorised.
Approved for a named surface after evidence and sign-off; not used in MC-14.

approvalWorkflow.action: Author drafts the claim with its intended audience and channel, and cites the evidence artefact or records NONE.
Classify A/C/P/X and set publicationStatus using the audience gate; internal and public contexts are separate decisions.
Check against the mandatory prohibited categories and the active hard restrictions; a Class A internal claim is not automatically a public claim.
Class C: attach the evidence record, obtain the approver sign-off and confirm the release gate is open. Until then the claim stays INTERNAL_ONLY and cannot be used publicly.
Independent review verifies the claim against the evidence artefact, not against a summary.
Any claim in a signed commercial document additionally requires the human signatory named in the brand/legal decision package.
Re-review every claim when a product lifecycle state, licence, certification, price or support period changes.

evidenceRules: A claim record must cite the exact evidence file, certificate, test report, signed contract or measurement; a design document alone is not product evidence.
No claim may be published from a hypothesis, internal model, scenario or roadmap entry.
Absence of evidence is never evidence of absence: an unverified status stays unverified.
Evidence must exist at the time of publication and be retained with the claim record.
Numbers in claims must match the approved source exactly, including units, currency, VAT basis and scope.

inheritedPolicyConflict.sourceStatement: Class A allows 'MAREA is a product brand of EMBARCARTE' and naming/edition statements today.
inheritedPolicyConflict.resolution: The stricter gate prevails in MC-14: no public MAREA brand use. MC-03 evidence is not edited; a formal supersession proposal is recorded in the decision log/delivery record and requires brand-owner and counsel approval.

internalVsPublic.internalNaming: MAREA may be used as an internal product name in planning, engineering and governance documents marked internal.
internalVsPublic.internalConceptDescription: Concept and defined-functionality statements are allowed only in internal documentation and must state that the product is DEFINED/not available.
internalVsPublic.customerFacing: No MAREA-branded customer-facing statement is authorised in MC-14.

enforcement.scope: Machine-verifiable conditions only: class/status vocabularies, prohibited categories blocked, bilingual parity, evidence presence for publication approval, hard restrictions.
enforcement.limitation: A keyword scanner cannot prove legal compliance; ambiguous claims require human legal review. Passing the validator is not a publication approval or a legal clearance.
enforcement.incidentHandling: A published claim found unsupported must be retracted within 24 hours, recorded, and the product's commercial state reviewed.
